seasons.label: Fall Recruiting
seasons.subtitle: Fall Recruiting · Primary hiring cycle — most companies recruit here
seasons.tip: Fall is the main season. Apply online the same week you meet a recruiter — applications go stale fast.

seasons.label: Spring Recruiting
seasons.subtitle: Spring Recruiting · Second cycle — smaller class, less competition
seasons.tip: Spring fairs have fewer companies but also fewer students. Easier to get face time with recruiters.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.subtitle: Summer · Co-op programs & virtual fairs — niche but worth knowing
seasons.tip: Few formal fairs run in summer. Co-op schools (Northeastern, Drexel, RPI) are the exception. Use Handshake virtual fairs to fill the gap.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.subtitle: Winter · Sparse season — mostly virtual, early deadlines
seasons.tip: Almost no in-person fairs in December. Focus on online applications and virtual fairs. Some companies close 2027 summer applications before winter break.

fairs.tip: Largest engineering career fair in the US. Arrive early — lines form before doors open. Wear comfortable shoes; you'll walk miles.
Schedule changes fast — check the app the morning of. Priority lines move quickly; use UIUC career fair app to track booth wait times.
CMU's fair skews heavily toward AI/ML and quant finance. Recruiters here know what MCTS and transformers are — come ready to go deep technically.
Research teams from AI labs attend MIT specifically to recruit. Bring a one-page research summary if you have any ML project or paper.
Many Bay Area startups send their CTO, not just a recruiter — great for non-traditional conversations.
EECS-only fair means every company there wants CS/ML talent. Much more targeted than a general university fair.
Amazon and Microsoft are headquartered in Seattle — their recruiting presence at UW is enormous. Get there early for their booths.
Finance + tech hybrid — Wall Street quant firms and AI labs both recruit heavily at Cornell. Know which lane you're targeting before you go.
Automotive AI is uniquely strong here — Ford, GM, Rivian, and Waymo recruit harder at UMich than at almost any other school.

fairs.location: West Lafayette, IN — Elliott Hall of Music
fairs.tip: One of the largest engineering career fairs in the Midwest. Strong aerospace and manufacturing AI presence alongside traditional tech.

fairs.fairName: UT Austin Engineering & CS Career Fair
fairs.tip: Austin's tech scene has exploded — Apple, Tesla, and Dell all have major Austin campuses and recruit aggressively here.

fairs.location: Los Angeles, CA — Ackerman Grand Ballroom
fairs.tip: Entertainment and defense AI companies show up at UCLA that you won't see at other fairs — Riot Games, Activision Blizzard, and Northrop all recruit here.

fairs.location: La Jolla, CA — Price Center Ballroom
fairs.tip: Qualcomm and defense/telecom companies have a strong presence unique to UCSD — valuable if you're interested in embedded AI or on-device ML.
Penn's Wharton + Engineering combo means finance-tech companies show up that don't attend pure engineering fairs. FinTech and AI for finance are strong.
NYC location means heavy quant finance + AI presence. Bloomberg terminal expertise is a differentiator for data-focused roles here.
Small school, small fair — but recruiter-to-student ratio is exceptionally high. NASA JPL and SpaceX target Caltech harder than any other school.
Quant finance and AI research firms recruit intensively. D.E. Shaw and Renaissance often interview directly on campus after the fair.
Harvard's SEAS is smaller than MIT, but the consulting + tech combo is strong. McKinsey, Bain, and BCG all attend and are increasingly interested in AI talent.
SAS Institute and Lenovo have strong Duke ties — data analytics and enterprise AI roles come through Duke more than most schools.
Healthcare AI is uniquely strong at Northwestern — Baxter, Abbott, and Northwestern Medicine recruit heavily here for biomedical AI roles.

fairs.location: Baltimore, MD — Ralph O'Connor Recreation Center
fairs.tip: Government and defense AI dominates JHU's fair — MITRE, APL, and Booz Allen are massive recruiters. Top school for AI in healthcare and national security.
Energy AI is a genuine differentiator at Rice — oil & gas companies are investing heavily in ML for seismic analysis and predictive maintenance.

fairs.location: Los Angeles, CA — Cromwell Track & Field
fairs.tip: Entertainment AI is USC's unique edge — Netflix, DreamWorks, and Disney Studios all recruit at USC for roles in recommendation systems and visual effects AI.
NYU's NYC location brings media-tech companies that don't recruit elsewhere — Spotify, Etsy, and media AI companies have strong ties to NYU Tandon.
Healthcare + biotech AI is strong at WashU due to the medical school connection. Express Scripts and Centene recruit specifically for health data ML roles.
One of the largest fairs on the East Coast. Defense and government AI contractors are dominant — strong for security clearance roles.
Epic Systems is the dominant recruiter and hires massively here — if you're interested in healthcare AI, Epic is a strong entry point with real ML projects.
Honda's R&D center is in Ohio — autonomous vehicle and robotics roles are uniquely strong. Intel also hires significantly at OSU for chip AI.

fairs.location: College Park, MD — Stamp Student Union
fairs.tip: UMD's DC proximity means federal AI and national security roles are everywhere. NSA, DHS, and intelligence agencies all recruit here alongside tech companies.

fairs.location: State College, PA — Bryce Jordan Center
fairs.tip: Penn State runs one of the largest single-day career fairs in the US. Arrive when doors open — the biggest booths have 1+ hour lines by noon.
Largest engineering school enrollment in the US means enormous fair. Energy sector AI is dominant — if you want to work on ML for oil & gas, this is the fair.

fairs.location: West Lafayette, IN — Lawson Computer Science Building
fairs.tip: CS-specific fair separate from the main engineering fair. Smaller, but recruiters are specifically there for software — much higher conversion rate per conversation.

fairs.location: Irvine, CA — Student Center Crystal Cove
fairs.tip: Blizzard, Broadcom, and Edwards Lifesciences recruit heavily at UCI specifically — strong for game AI, semiconductor AI, and medical device ML.
UCSB has a strong local startup scene — regional companies you won't find at other fairs often attend and are easier to get time with.
National labs (Lawrence Livermore, Lawrence Berkeley) recruit at Davis for AI research roles that rarely appear at other university fairs.

fairs.location: Gainesville, FL — Stephen C. O'Connell Center
fairs.tip: Florida's aerospace and defense cluster is strong — Harris and Lockheed have massive Gainesville/Orlando presence and recruit hard at UF.
SAS Institute is headquartered in Cary, NC — they recruit massive numbers from NC State for analytics and ML engineering roles. Also IBM Red Hat is local.
Medtronic and UnitedHealth are Minneapolis-based and recruit massively here for healthcare AI. 3M also has strong ML research roles.
Northeastern's co-op reputation means companies come here specifically looking for students who can start quickly. Emphasize your availability timeline.
IBM has deep historical ties to RPI — many AI research and systems roles come through here. GE's AI research also recruits specifically at RPI.
Space and atmospheric science AI are uniquely strong at CU Boulder — Ball Aerospace, NCAR, and NOAA all recruit here for ML in satellite and climate data.
Biotech and pharma AI companies attend BU specifically because of the medical campus — Biogen, Takeda, and others recruit for AI drug discovery.
Virtual fairs let you reach companies not recruiting at your school. Schedule 10-min slots in advance — drop-ins rarely get quality time.
Spring at GT is still one of the biggest in the country. Many companies who filled tech headcount in fall return in spring for engineering and operations roles.
Spring at MIT draws biotech and govtech companies that don't attend the fall fair. If you're interested in AI for science, spring is the right fair.
CMU spring skews toward AI startups and autonomous vehicle companies — smaller and scrappier than the fall fair, excellent for research-focused roles.

fairs.location: Berkeley, CA — MLK Jr. Student Union
fairs.tip: Berkeley spring has a strong consumer tech and product-focused company mix. Good fair if you're exploring PM or product analytics roles alongside SWE.
UIUC spring is still one of the largest spring fairs in the Midwest. Companies returning in spring often have more flexibility on start dates.
Spring in Seattle is when companies have clearer headcount numbers — easier to get concrete timelines from recruiters than in the fall chaos.
Cornell spring draws many of the same firms as fall. Good second-chance opportunity if you missed a company in fall or want more conversations.
Spring is when automotive companies return to fill co-op and new-grad roles that opened up after fall headcount solidified.
Capital One's AI division is a standout spring recruiter at VT — excellent entry point for finance AI if you're interested in consumer lending or fraud ML.

fairs.fairName: UT Austin Spring Engineering Career Fair
fairs.tip: Austin's tech community grows every year — spring is when many Austin-based startups attend who couldn't afford fall fair booth fees.

fairs.location: West Lafayette, IN — Elliott Hall of Music
fairs.tip: Eli Lilly attends specifically for pharmaceutical AI and ML roles — Purdue is one of their top recruiting schools for data science.
Northeastern's co-op model means this fair has companies actively looking to hire students for 6-month co-op rotations starting in January or July — very concrete opportunities.
JPMorgan Chase has a large Columbus tech hub and recruits heavily at OSU in spring for data science and AI roles in financial services.

fairs.location: Los Angeles, CA — Cromwell Track & Field
fairs.tip: Spring at USC draws more entertainment and streaming AI companies — Netflix and Hulu both attend specifically to recruit for recommendation systems and personalization.
Consulting and finance companies doing AI transformation work recruit heavily at spring virtual fairs. Worth attending if you're open to AI strategy or analyst roles.
Drexel's quarter system means students enter and exit co-ops in July. Summer fair is specifically for the July–December co-op cycle — very concrete, near-term roles.
Northeastern's unique co-op program has more students entering the workforce in summer than any other school. Less competition than fall — companies often hire 100% of booth conversations.

fairs.location: San Luis Obispo, CA — Recreation Center
fairs.tip: Cal Poly's 'learn by doing' reputation makes it unusually attractive to companies looking for students who can contribute from day one. Strong hands-on project portfolio matters here.
Summer virtual fairs fill gaps left by the fall/spring cycles. Most useful for students who missed fall recruiting or switched majors. Less competitive but also fewer elite-company spots.

fairs.location: Troy, NY — East Campus Athletic Village
fairs.tip: RPI's summer event is smaller and more networking-focused than a traditional fair — bring a sharper, more targeted pitch. Regeneron attends for biotech AI roles not found elsewhere.
One of the few recruitment events in December. Companies attending winter virtual fairs have urgent headcount — response rates are high. Apply before winter break; roles close fast.
IAP (Independent Activities Period) events attract research-focused companies specifically scouting for students with strong technical projects. Portfolio-first conversations.
CMU's December event is small and research-focused. Autonomous vehicle and robotics companies attend specifically because CMU's Robotics Institute is the #1 program in the country.
Northeastern's January co-op cycle requires a December fair — this is one of the few in-person winter events in the country. MathWorks attends almost exclusively here for MATLAB AI tools roles.

fairs.location: Gainesville, FL — Reitz Union Grand Ballroom
fairs.tip: Florida's January fair is between true winter and spring cycles — companies attending are often hiring for immediate starts or summer. Good for students graduating in May.

prepTips.label: 30-Second Elevator Pitch
prepTips.detail: Prepare a crisp intro: name, school, major, one project, one goal. Practice it out loud until it sounds natural, not rehearsed. Recruiters hear hundreds of pitches — clarity and energy stand out.

prepTips.label: Research Before You Go
prepTips.detail: Look up each company's careers page and current open roles the night before. At the booth, mention the specific role by name. 'I saw your ML infrastructure team is hiring' beats 'I'm interested in tech jobs.'

prepTips.label: Follow Up the Same Day
prepTips.detail: Email or LinkedIn message within 24 hours — reference something specific from your conversation. 'Great talking about your work on recommendation systems' is far more memorable than a generic note.

prepTips.label: Apply Online in Parallel
prepTips.detail: Meeting a recruiter at a fair does not replace the online application. Submit your application the same evening. Write the recruiter's name in the referral field if the form has one.
